title: JavaScript Design Patterns Applied Check
description: Apply JavaScript design patterns to realistic code examples and choose simple designs that avoid over-engineering.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which pattern best fits this problem: user objects are created in many files with different default properties?
questions.explanation: A factory centralizes creation so user objects have a consistent shape.
The code chooses from interchangeable shipping algorithms at runtime.

options.text: It exposes broad mutable global state

questions.explanation: Many files can mutate this shared object, making changes hard to trace.

questions.prompt:
Which code is the best adapter for API user data?
```js
const apiUser = { user_id: 1, full_name: "Ada" };
```
questions.explanation: The adapter converts external field names into the app's internal shape.

options.text: It does not return the wrapped function's result
It logs before calling the function

questions.explanation: A wrapper should usually preserve the original return value with `return fn(...args)`.

questions.prompt: Which pattern is most appropriate for many parts of an app reacting when `cart:item-added` happens?
questions.explanation: Observer and pub/sub patterns notify listeners when events occur.

questions.prompt: What should a `subscribe()` method usually return?
questions.explanation: Returning an unsubscribe function makes cleanup clear and helps avoid memory leaks.

questions.prompt: Which design is easiest to test?

options.text: `loadUser(id, apiClient)` where the API client is passed in
`loadUser(id)` that always imports and uses the real API client
`loadUser()` that reads a global user ID and real API client
`loadUser()` that writes directly to the DOM

questions.explanation: Passing the dependency allows tests to provide a fake API client.

questions.prompt: What pattern best fits a drawing app that stores actions so users can undo them?
questions.explanation: Commands can represent actions with `execute` and `undo` behavior.
A generator function creates an iterator/iterable that yields values one at a time.

options.text: `saveSettings(settings)` that validates, serializes, stores, and publishes the change
`utils(value)` that does unrelated work based on many flags
An object that exposes every private helper
A function that renames one API field

questions.explanation: A facade provides one simple operation over a coherent set of internal steps.

questions.prompt: A team has one small `if` statement with two short cases that are unlikely to grow. What is usually best?

options.text: Create a large strategy framework immediately
Move all state into a singleton

questions.explanation: Patterns should solve real complexity. A simple conditional can be the clearest design.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of composition?

options.text: Creating an order service from injected `paymentService` and `emailService`
Making every service inherit from one huge parent class
Keeping all app behavior in one object
Reading every dependency from global variables

questions.explanation: Composition builds larger behavior by combining smaller collaborators.

options.text: A tiny feature requires many managers, factories, strategies, and commands with no clear benefit
Duplicated object creation was extracted into a small factory
External API data is adapted at the boundary
A listener returns an unsubscribe function

questions.explanation: Stacking patterns without improving clarity is pattern soup and should be simplified.
